location: Preparations; A Game Round / Players’ Choices; credits
firstPlayerRule: Everyone makes their explore-or-return decision simultaneously. Choose a Guide, preferably someone who already knows the game, to coordinate play.
clarifications: The Guide prepares the round and signals when everyone reveals their decision. This role does not give that person an earlier decision than the other explorers.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 1, 2 and 4 inspected. This is the ©2018 meeple-based file, distinct from the ©2024 Explore/Exit-card rules in the same publisher-linked folder. The endgame scoring tie-break is not a starting tie-break.

location: Opening explanation and Setup; simultaneous Explore/Exit decisions; credits
firstPlayerRule: Players take their turns simultaneously. Pick a Guide to manage the Temple cards and coordinate the phases; there is no individual first explorer.
clarifications: Players reveal their Explore or Exit cards together when the Guide gives the signal.
This file does not specify a personal criterion for choosing the Guide. The older ©2018 rules prefer someone familiar with the game; that preference is not stated here.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 1, 3 and 4 inspected. The visible copyright is ©2024; the extracted production footer says INCAN GOLD RULES 2023 v7. Edition is identified by visible copyright and Explore/Exit cards, not inferred from a product upload date.

editionLabel: Eagle-Gryphon English rules, ©2020, publisher’s six-page Preview file
location: Setup step 7; Playing the Game; credits; Solo Challenges
firstPlayerRule: Whoever last visited a market takes the first turn.
clarifications: Play then proceeds clockwise.
With four players, the fourth player receives the extra Pub tile during setup.
This starting criterion applies to multiplayer games. The included solo challenges have separate setup instructions.
evidenceNotes: All six pages of the image-only PDF were rendered and visually read. The text extractor returned empty pages, so the answer comes from the visible setup passage, not an inferred search snippet.

editionLabel: Eagle-Gryphon English V8 public rulebook, Explor8 ©2022, linked from the Deluxe edition
location: How to Play / Ambassador Phase; President’s Office; credits
firstPlayerRule: Agree on a method for choosing the starter. Give the chosen player the President of the Senate pawn; they begin the Ambassador phase.
houseFallback: Your group may agree to choose randomly; the rulebook leaves the selection method to everyone’s agreement.
clarifications: Before play, players choose Starting tiles counterclockwise, beginning with the person to the starter’s right. This is a setup draft, separate from the clockwise Ambassador turns.
The President’s Office action can change who starts the next round.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 7, 20 and 32 inspected. The two-page Deluxe insert was also rendered and read; it adds components and bonus tiles but directs players to normal setup and does not replace the starting instruction. That insert is cached as federation-7e97a332.pdf. No themed personal-history criterion is supplied in the inspected English rulebook.

editionLabel: Eagle-Gryphon English Preview rulebook, ©2019, April 2020 production file
location: Starting turn-order spaces; Colonization Phase; Solo Game; First Colonists variant and credits
firstPlayerRule: The player with the most viewings of The Martian chooses a turn-order space first. After everyone chooses, the lowest occupied numbered space takes the first Colonization turn.
clarifications: Turn-order spaces are chosen clockwise from that initial chooser. The first chooser is not necessarily first to take a Colonization action.
The First Colonists variant assigns spaces using randomly dealt tiles instead of letting players choose their spaces.
Solo setup assigns Lacerda’s space with a random First Colonists tile, then lets you choose your own space or randomize it.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 7, 8, 22 and 24 inspected. Copyright is ©2019 and extracted production footer is dated April 27, 2020. The reference book was retrieved as supporting material but is not needed to support the summarized starting order.

location: Setup after step 6; Move Workers / Turn Order; solo variant and credits
firstPlayerRule: The person who last bought a robot starts the first worker-placement phase. You may instead choose that player randomly.
officialTieBreak: Random selection is an official alternative; it is not restricted to a tie.
clarifications: Initial worker placement proceeds clockwise. After that first placement phase, turn order follows the workers’ positions from left to right, including Sandra.
During setup, the initial last player receives an extra Speech token and players take their first Part tiles in reverse turn order.
The personal-history criterion selects among players in the multiplayer game; the solo Inspection variant has its own setup.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 3, 4, 10, 11 and 12 inspected. The criterion selects the initial Move Workers turn, not necessarily the first subsequent Perform Actions turn. The file explicitly offers random selection.

location: Player Setup step M; phase sequence; City phase; Turn Order phase; credits
firstPlayerRule: The rulebook names whoever most recently robbed a bank as the initial starter. That player leads the opening City-tile placement; the order reverses before the first Player Action phase.
clarifications: Setup records the initial order clockwise from that player.
The Turn Order phase ranks players by Notoriety, with ties reversing the tied players’ existing order. Everyone is initially tied, so the first day’s action order is the reverse of the setup order.
In the two-player setup, Sandra occupies the third initial position on the turn-order track.
interpretation: The bank-robbery line is the rulebook’s thematic starting criterion. The inspected passage supplies no substitute for a group to which it does not apply; an agreed random choice below is a house rule.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 inspected. The initial starter is distinguished from the Player Action starter; the source explicitly says Day 1 order reverses because all Notoriety values are tied. The visible two-player setup puts Sandra in position 3. No invented official fallback or real-world qualification was added.

editionLabel: Eagle-Gryphon English public rules, ©2023, v10 production file
location: Setup step 3; Stone Age setup round; How to Play; Era Change; two-player setup; credits
firstPlayerRule: With three or four players, whoever most recently invented something takes the first position in turn order. With two players, randomize the order of both players and Chronos.
clarifications: In the three- or four-player game, initial turn order proceeds clockwise from the selected player.
The preliminary Stone Age setup round runs in reverse turn order. It is separate from the regular turns that follow.
Turn order can change later under the Era Change procedure.
evidenceNotes: Rendered pages 2, 4, 7, 10, 22 and 23 inspected. The two-player exception explicitly randomizes both players and automated opponent Chronos; it is not a starting tie-break for the three- or four-player criterion. The separate solo rulebook was not imported or represented as reviewed.
